title: Nested array mixed with a scalar - the base key is the contract, the collision is refused
rationale: This exact document appears in the MapFlattener class javadoc. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS FIELD, made 2026-08-19. (1) It used to say the javadoc claimed the output was data_name plus data_value. That was false at HEAD: commit 6bb66d1 rewrote the javadoc block to describe the measured output, and this sentence was one of the two sites the false premise survived in - SentinelKeyProseMatchesTheCodeTest now bans it by substring. (2) The sentinel key is no longer an open question. [BL-022] DECIDED it: the base key is the contract and a _value-suffixed column is REFUSED, because joinEncodedKey does not re-escape an already-encoded field name, so a user field literally named `value` produces the identical key - see the sibling fixture mixed-array-sentinel-vs-user-value-field, which measures both collisions the rename would create. What remains DEFECT here is the reconstruct side: the flat key set {data, data_name} is injective and loses nothing, and a reader that zips the two columns by outer index recovers the source exactly. Nothing does that zip yet.
catchesBugClass: The leaf-versus-branch key collision in setNestedValue, where a one-segment key and a longer key sharing it as a prefix cannot both be represented in the reconstructed tree. Since 2.1.0 ([BL-023]) that is REFUSED with KeyCollisionException instead of being decided by map iteration order, so this row now catches 'the refusal stopped happening' rather than 'the clobber picked a different winner'. It NO LONGER catches 'documentation that describes a padding control that was never implemented' (closed by [BL-018] in 2.1.0) nor 'the javadoc documents data_value' (corrected in 6bb66d1).
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the reverse collision order, because the outcome no longer depends on order at all - JsonReconstructorKeyCollisionTest owns that invariant and feeds both orders explicitly. It cannot catch the collision arising with NO sentinel involved; structural/nullable-nested-record-shadowed-json-stack exists for that. It cannot catch the flatten-side collisions a _value suffix would create, which is what structural/mixed-array-sentinel-vs-user-value-field measures - the fix must NOT be to rename the column. It does not measure the positional contract in isolation either: MapFlattenerNestedArrayAlignmentTest owns that, and its two strings for this document must stay identical to the ones recorded here. THE PREVIOUS VERSION OF THIS FIELD instructed that the fix must not be to edit the javadoc to match the code; 6bb66d1 did exactly that and did it well, keeping the discrepancy legible rather than erasing it, so the instruction was already violated by a good change and is replaced rather than obeyed.

predicted.detail: Flatten is CORRECT and unchanged: the sentinel column is emitted under the base key 'data' at both emit sites, deliberately ([BL-022]), and {data, data_name} is an injective encoding of two columns of one array. The positional half was repaired in 2.1.0 ([BL-018]). What remains DEFECT is the RECONSTRUCT side. Until 2.1.0 setNestedValue resolved the resulting leaf/branch collision by map iteration order and silently dropped data_name; since [BL-023] it refuses with KeyCollisionException, which is deterministic and loud but still does not reproduce the source. The repair that would make this row LOSSLESS is zipping the base column with the field columns by outer index; that is not implemented.
